title: Universal at Halloween
titleTail: : Horror Nights on Both Coasts, and What It Costs
h1: Universal at Halloween: Horror Nights on both coasts, and who should not buy a ticket
description: Halloween Horror Nights in Orlando and Hollywood compared: when each season runs, which nights are cheap, and why this is not a family Halloween.
summary: In 2026, Halloween Horror Nights runs at Universal Studios Florida on 49 select nights from August 28 through November 1 and at Universal Studios Hollywood on 42 select nights from September 3 through November 1. Both are separately ticketed horror events; choose the coast, date and ticket type before planning the rest of the trip.

typicalWindow.startsAround: late August or early September in Orlando, early September in Hollywood
typicalWindow.endsAround: the first weekend of November at both resorts

sections.heading: The short answer
body: Start with an actual 2026 event date: Orlando runs 49 select nights from August 28 through November 1; Hollywood runs 42 select nights from September 3 through November 1. Both require a separate Halloween Horror Nights ticket. Daytime park admission, event Express and early entry are separate decisions, with different products by coast.

The events run at Universal Studios Florida and Universal Studios Hollywood on select nights, with separate event admission and event Express. Orlando has ten houses and a larger resort; Hollywood has eight houses and the Terror Tram on the working backlot. Check the official date calendar before booking, since the ranges do not mean every night is an event night.

The decision rule that covers most people: if you are travelling for the event, go on a weeknight before the middle of October and pick Orlando. If the event is an add-on to a Los Angeles trip you were taking anyway, Hollywood is the obvious choice and one night is enough.

sections.heading: This is not a family Halloween, and Universal does not pretend it is
body: Halloween Horror Nights is a mature-audience horror event. Universal does not recommend it for children under thirteen. Families can still visit the parks by day and should check the official park and entertainment calendars for seasonal offerings; those are distinct from admission to the nighttime event.

This is the single largest difference between Universal's autumn and the one down the road in Orlando, and it catches families every year. A household that wants a costume-and-candy evening at a theme park will not find one here at any price, on either coast.

Daytime park operations and seasonal entertainment differ by resort and date. Halloween Horror Nights admission does not replace a daytime park ticket, and a daytime ticket does not include Halloween Horror Nights. Check the official calendar and ticket terms for the visit date.

sections.heading: What the nights cost, and why the date matters more than anything else
body: 2026 Halloween Horror Nights tickets and event Express are date-priced. Check the official ticket calendar for your selected night and compare the total for your group, including tax and add-ons. Prior-year price bands are not current quotes.

The same date curve applies to the event's Express Pass, which is sold separately from the daytime version and is the most expensive queue product Universal offers. On a peak Saturday it is close to necessary if you want to see most of the houses; on an early-season weeknight it is genuinely optional.

Put those two together and the arithmetic that most first-time attendees miss becomes obvious. Two cheap weeknights usually cost less than one peak Saturday with Express Pass, and they deliver far more houses. Buying the date rather than the upgrade is the strongest move available in this season.

Multi-night and season-long event passes exist at both resorts and are worth pricing if you intend more than two nights, because the marginal night on those products costs much less than a second single-night ticket. They carry blockout dates on the busiest nights, which is exactly what you would expect.

sections.heading: When each season actually runs
body: The 2026 dates are confirmed: Orlando runs August 28 through November 1 on 49 select nights, and Hollywood runs September 3 through November 1 on 42 select nights. The published event-night calendars, rather than these start and end dates alone, decide whether a particular evening is eligible.

Neither resort runs the event nightly. Early in the season it is weekends plus a handful of weeknights; by October it is most nights of the week. That structure is why the first weeks are both cheaper and quieter, and it is also why a trip in the last week of August can miss the season entirely on the wrong dates.
The 2026 schedules are published. Use each resort’s official event ticket calendar to select a real event night and check its event hours before buying travel.

sections.heading: Which coast, decided honestly
body: Pick Orlando if the event is the trip. It runs more houses, more scare zones and more nights, the park is large enough to absorb a sold-out crowd, and the surrounding resort gives you two other theme parks to fill the days with while you sleep off the nights. It is also the version where a multi-night pass makes sense.

Pick Hollywood if you are already in Los Angeles or if the weather matters. Valley evenings in October fall into the high 50s, which is the best night-event weather either resort produces, and the event's use of the backlot — including a Halloween version of the tram experience — is something Orlando has no equivalent for.

The thing that decides it for most people is not content but stamina. Orlando's event rewards multiple nights and Hollywood's is a single excellent night. If you have one evening, the coasts are close; if you have three, Orlando wins clearly.

sections.heading: How to work a night, whichever coast you pick
body: Be at the gate for the event opening and go to the furthest houses first. Almost every attendee works from the entrance outward, which makes the queue pattern predictable and the far end of the park the cheapest place to spend the first hour.

Do not plan a full daytime park day before an event night. The event runs late, the houses involve a lot of walking, and the standard mistake is arriving at the gate already tired. On event dates the host park closes early to daytime guests anyway, so a full day there is not on offer.

Eat before the event or early in it. Food queues inside the event get worse as the night goes on and are competing for the same hours as the houses. The same applies to merchandise, which is the other queue nobody budgets time for.

universal-orlando.verdict: One weeknight early in the season, with the daytime spent at the two parks that do not host the event.
universal-orlando.note: The 2026 event at Universal Studios Florida runs August 28–November 1 on 49 select nights with ten houses. A separate event ticket is required. Islands of Adventure and Epic Universe do not host Halloween Horror Nights; check their own daytime calendars for any seasonal entertainment. Use the official event date and price calendar for the night you want.

universal-hollywood.verdict: One night, in far better weather than Orlando, as an add-on to a Los Angeles trip rather than a destination.
universal-hollywood.note: The 2026 event at Universal Studios Hollywood runs September 3–November 1 on 42 select nights with eight houses and the Terror Tram. A separate event ticket is required. General Admission excludes Hollywood Drift; Universal's event announcement lists some premium and Day/Night products as including it, while a current Express ticket terms page says Express excludes it. Check the exact ticket product, event calendar and confirmation for your selected night.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum age for Halloween Horror Nights?
faqs.a: Universal does not enforce one at either resort, and it states clearly that the event is not recommended for children under thirteen. That is guidance rather than a rule, and the practical answer is that the houses are designed to frighten adults and the walkways are worked by performers whose job is to startle people. If you would not take a child to a horror film, do not take them to this.

faqs.q: Do I need a daytime park ticket as well as an event ticket?
faqs.a: No. The event ticket admits you to the host park for the event hours, and on event nights that park closes early to daytime guests and reopens for ticket holders. Buying a full day ticket for the same date is only worth it if you want the daytime hours as well, and on a Horror Nights date those hours are shortened. Most people are better off taking a different park during the day.

faqs.q: Is the event Express Pass worth buying?
faqs.a: On the last three weekends before Halloween, yes, if seeing most of the houses matters to you, because standby queues on those nights can run past an hour each. On a weeknight in September or early October, usually not — the first two hours of standby are short enough to clear several houses without it. It is sold separately from the daytime Express Pass and is priced by date.

faqs.q: Which resort has the better Halloween Horror Nights?
faqs.a: Orlando for scale and Hollywood for atmosphere. Orlando runs more houses across more nights in a bigger park, which makes it the better choice if you intend to do the whole list or attend more than one night. Hollywood is shorter, uses the working backlot in a way Orlando cannot, and runs in noticeably better weather. For a single night the two are close enough that travel logistics should decide it.

faqs.q: Are the current season's dates on this page confirmed?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2026 season ranges are confirmed: Orlando August 28–November 1 (49 select nights), Hollywood September 3–November 1 (42 select nights). Those are ranges, not nightly schedules. Confirm your intended date on the official event ticket calendar before buying travel.

faqs.q: Is there anything at Universal at Halloween for a family with a six-year-old?
faqs.a: Halloween Horror Nights is not recommended for children under thirteen. For a family trip, use the daytime park calendar to see which seasonal entertainment is offered on your date, and do not treat an event ticket as ordinary daytime admission.
